title: Immunoinformatic Design and Structural Evaluation of a Full-Length mRNA Vaccine Targeting Rabies Glycoprotein G
abstract: Background/Objectives: Rabies remains a fatal viral disease, and current conventional vaccine strategies face significant challenges regarding structural stability and large-scale manufacturing. This study aimed to design a novel messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccine candidate targeting the rabies virus glycoprotein G (RABV-G) using an integrated immunoinformatic and structural modeling framework. Methods: The RABV-G sequence was systematically evaluated for evolutionary conservation and safety, followed by 3D structural modeling. Highly antigenic B-cell and T-cell epitopes were identified based on human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding, toxicity, and glycosylation shielding analyses. Functional interactions were assessed via molecular docking with the Toll-like Receptor 4/Myeloid Differentiation factor 2 (TLR4-MD2) complex. Finally, a full-length mRNA construct was engineered and computationally evaluated for translational efficiency, structural stability, and immune simulation. Results: The RABV-G target exhibited high evolutionary conservation, with 53.82% of positions fully identical and an additional 43.70% highly conserved (70–99%) across 87 analyzed sequences. Structural validation confirmed a high-quality model, enabling the extraction of accessible, non-glycosylated epitopes. Molecular docking simulations revealed a highly favorable predicted structural interaction with the TLR4-MD2 receptor, suggesting a potential structural capacity to engage innate immune pathways, pending experimental validation. The codon-optimized mRNA construct exhibited a predicted thermodynamically stable secondary structure (MFE = −429.50 kcal/mol) with an accessible translation initiation site, pending experimental validation. Furthermore, in silico immune simulations predicted a robust and sustained activation of both humoral and cellular immunity, notably including memory B-cell expansion. Conclusions: The computationally designed mRNA vaccine candidate demonstrates highly favorable structural characteristics and immunogenic potential. While these in silico findings present a promising foundational framework for rabies prevention, subsequent experimental laboratory validation is strictly required to confirm its functional efficacy and translation.

This study aimed to design a novel messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccine candidate targeting the rabies virus glycoprotein G (RABV-G) using an integrated immunoinformatic and structural modeling framework. Methods: The RABV-G sequence was systematically evaluated for evolutionary conservation and safety, followed by 3D structural modeling. Highly antigenic B-cell and T-cell epitopes were identified based on human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding, toxicity, and glycosylation shielding analyses. Functional interactions were assessed via molecular docking with the Toll-like Receptor 4/Myeloid Differentiation factor 2 (TLR4-MD2) complex. Finally, a full-length mRNA construct was engineered and computationally evaluated for translational efficiency, structural stability, and immune simulation. Results: The RABV-G target exhibited high evolutionary conservation, with 53.82% of positions fully identical and an additional 43.70% highly conserved (70–99%) across 87 analyzed sequences. Structural validation confirmed a high-quality model, enabling the extraction of accessible, non-glycosylated epitopes. Molecular docking simulations revealed a highly favorable predicted structural interaction with the TLR4-MD2 receptor, suggesting a potential structural capacity to engage innate immune pathways, pending experimental validation. The codon-optimized mRNA construct exhibited a predicted thermodynamically stable secondary structure (MFE = −429.50 kcal/mol) with an accessible translation initiation site, pending experimental validation. Furthermore, in silico immune simulations predicted a robust and sustained activation of both humoral and cellular immunity, notably including memory B-cell expansion. Conclusions: The computationally designed mRNA vaccine candidate demonstrates highly favorable structural characteristics and immunogenic potential. While these in silico findings present a promising foundational framework for rabies prevention, subsequent experimental laboratory validation is strictly required to confirm its functional efficacy and translation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 狂犬病 仍然是一种致命的病毒性疾病,当前传统的 疫苗 策略在结构稳定性和大规模制造方面面临着重大挑战。本研究旨在使用集成的免疫信息学和结构建模框架设计一种针对 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白 G (RABV-G) 的新型信使核糖核酸 (mRNA) 疫苗 候选物。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用计算机模拟方法进行,重点关注 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白 G (RABV-G) 及其结构和免疫原性特性。该研究涉及对 87 个 RABV-G 分析序列进行评估,以评估进化保守性和安全性。
elements_zh.methods: 对 RABV-G 序列的进化保守性和安全性进行了系统评估,然后进行 3D 结构建模。基于人类白细胞抗原 (HLA) 结合、毒性和糖基化屏蔽分析,鉴定了高抗原性 B 细胞和 T 细胞表位。通过与 Toll 样受体 4/骨髓分化因子 2 (TLR4-MD2) 复合物的分子对接来评估功能相互作用。设计了全长 mRNA 构建体,并通过计算评估了翻译效率、结构稳定性和免疫模拟。
elements_zh.main_results: RABV-G 靶标表现出高度的进化保守性,在 87 个分析序列中,53.82% 的位置完全相同,另外 43.70% 的位置高度保守 (70-99%)。结构验证证实了高质量模型,能够提取可接近的非糖基化表位。分子对接模拟揭示了与 TLR4-MD2 受体的高度有利的预测结构相互作用,表明其具有参与先天免疫途径的潜在结构能力,有待实验验证。密码子优化的 mRNA 构建体表现出预测的热力学稳定二级结构 (MFE = -429.50 kcal/mol) 和可访问的翻译起始位点,有待实验验证。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 计算设计的 mRNA 疫苗 候选物表现出非常有利的结构特征和免疫原性潜力。这些计算机研究结果为 狂犬病 预防提供了一个有前途的基础框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为开发针对 狂犬病 的新 mRNA 疫苗 提供了有希望的基础,这可以提高结构稳定性和大规模生产。该结果可能为未来 疫苗 设计和免疫原性的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算机分析,需要随后的实验实验室验证以确认功能功效和翻译。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于计算模型而不是经验数据。

Finally, a full-length mRNA construct was engineered and computationally evaluated for translational efficiency, structural stability, and immune simulation. Results: The RABV-G target exhibited high evolutionary conservation, with 53.82% of positions fully identical and an additional 43.70% highly conserved (70–99%) across 87 analyzed sequences. Structural validation confirmed a high-quality model, enabling the extraction of accessible, non-glycosylated epitopes. Molecular docking simulations revealed a highly favorable predicted structural interaction with the TLR4-MD2 receptor, suggesting a potential structural capacity to engage innate immune pathways, pending experimental validation. The codon-optimized mRNA construct exhibited a predicted thermodynamically stable secondary structure (MFE = −429.50 kcal/mol) with an accessible translation initiation site, pending experimental validation. Furthermore, in silico immune simulations predicted a robust and sustained activation of both humoral and cellular immunity, notably including memory B-cell expansion. Conclusions: The computationally designed mRNA vaccine candidate demonstrates highly favorable structural characteristics and immunogenic potential. While these in silico findings present a promising foundational framework for rabies prevention, subsequent experimental laboratory validation is strictly required to confirm its functional efficacy and translation.

title: Rabies Prevention in Practice, Awareness, Immediate Bite Response, Care-Seeking, and Barriers among Grade 5 Pupils and Their Parents in a Selected Public Elementary School in San Pablo City, Laguna
abstract: Rabies remains a critical public health concern in the Philippines, particularly among school-aged children who are at increased risk because of frequent contact with domestic and stray animals. This study assessed the awareness, immediate bite response, care-seeking behavior, and perceived barriers to rabies prevention among Grade 5 pupils and their parents in San Pablo City, Laguna. A descriptive, comparative, and cross-sectional research design was employed, involving 302 Grade 5 pupils and their corresponding parents. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire that examined participants’ knowledge of rabies transmission, prevention practices, immediate wound management, care-seeking intentions, and barriers to treatment. Findings revealed that most participants demonstrated a high level of awareness regarding rabies, with 71.19% of pupils and 75.83% of parents recognizing dog bites as the primary mode of transmission. However, misconceptions persisted, particularly among pupils, regarding the possibility that apparently healthy animals could still transmit rabies. Although most respondents expressed a strong intention to seek medical care following an animal bite, with 90% of pupils and 85% of parents indicating they would visit a health facility, deficiencies remained in recommended first-aid practices, including proper wound washing and avoidance of traditional remedies. Financial constraints, reported by 60% of parents, fear of vaccination, and limited access to healthcare facilities were identified as the major barriers to timely treatment. The findings indicate that awareness alone is insufficient to ensure appropriate preventive behaviors. Strengthening school- and community-based health education, correcting misconceptions, improving access to affordable post-exposure prophylaxis, and promoting collaboration among healthcare providers, educational institutions, and local government units are essential to enhance rabies prevention and encourage timely responses to potential rabies exposure.
journal: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research

title_zh: Rabies Prevention in Practice, Awareness, Immediate Bite Response, Care-Seeking, and Barriers among Grade 5 Pupils and Their Parents in a Selected Public Elementary School in San Pablo City, Laguna
source_body_en: Rabies remains a critical public health concern in the Philippines, particularly among school-aged children who are at increased risk because of frequent contact with domestic and stray animals. This study assessed the awareness, immediate bite response, care-seeking behavior, and perceived barriers to rabies prevention among Grade 5 pupils and their parents in San Pablo City, Laguna. A descriptive, comparative, and cross-sectional research design was employed, involving 302 Grade 5 pupils and their corresponding parents. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire that examined participants’ knowledge of rabies transmission, prevention practices, immediate wound management, care-seeking intentions, and barriers to treatment. Findings revealed that most participants demonstrated a high level of awareness regarding rabies, with 71.19% of pupils and 75.83% of parents recognizing dog bites as the primary mode of transmission. However, misconceptions persisted, particularly among pupils, regarding the possibility that apparently healthy animals could still transmit rabies. Although most respondents expressed a strong intention to seek medical care following an animal bite, with 90% of pupils and 85% of parents indicating they would visit a health facility, deficiencies remained in recommended first-aid practices, including proper wound washing and avoidance of traditional remedies. Financial constraints, reported by 60% of parents, fear of vaccination, and limited access to healthcare facilities were identified as the major barriers to timely treatment. The findings indicate that awareness alone is insufficient to ensure appropriate preventive behaviors. Strengthening school- and community-based health education, correcting misconceptions, improving access to affordable post-exposure prophylaxis, and promoting collaboration among healthcare providers, educational institutions, and local government units are essential to enhance rabies prevention and encourage timely responses to potential rabies exposure.

title: Beneath the bark: mapping dog bite patterns and injury severity – a cross-sectional study at rural health training centre Santhpur, Bidar, Karnataka
abstract: Background: Rabies is a vaccine-preventable, zoonotic, viral disease that invariably affects the central nervous system, with dogs responsible for virus transmission in up to 99% of human cases. India remains endemic for rabies and accounts for approximately 36% of global rabies deaths. Objectives were to describe the pattern and severity of injuries among patients presenting with dog bite complaints to rural health training centre. Methods: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2026 to May 2026 at RHTC Santhpur, Bidar. All 63 patients presenting with dog bite complaints were enrolled and data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographic profiles, bite characteristics, wound categorization, and post-exposure management. Analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel 2022. Results: Of the 63 patients, 46 (73%) were male. The most affected age group was 6-25 years (42.86%). The majority of bites occurred in the evening (38.1%) and stray dogs accounted for (52.4%) of bites. Unprovoked bites were predominant (77.78%). Lower limbs were the most commonly bitten site (71.4%). Category II wounds predominated (85.7%), while category III wounds constituted (14.3%). First aid with soap and water was performed by (98.4%) of victims. However, only (11.1%) of category III patients received rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). Conclusions: Dog bites predominantly affect young, productive-age males, with a near-equal burden from stray and pet dogs. The critical gap in RIG availability for category III patients represents a serious public health concern requiring urgent systemic intervention.

title_zh: 树皮之下:绘制狗咬伤模式和伤害严重程度——卡纳塔克邦比达尔乡村健康培训中心桑斯布尔的一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Background: Rabies is a vaccine-preventable, zoonotic, viral disease that invariably affects the central nervous system, with dogs responsible for virus transmission in up to 99% of human cases. India remains endemic for rabies and accounts for approximately 36% of global rabies deaths. Objectives were to describe the pattern and severity of injuries among patients presenting with dog bite complaints to rural health training centre. Methods: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2026 to May 2026 at RHTC Santhpur, Bidar. All 63 patients presenting with dog bite complaints were enrolled and data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographic profiles, bite characteristics, wound categorization, and post-exposure management. Analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel 2022. Results: Of the 63 patients, 46 (73%) were male. The most affected age group was 6-25 years (42.86%). The majority of bites occurred in the evening (38.1%) and stray dogs accounted for (52.4%) of bites. Unprovoked bites were predominant (77.78%). Lower limbs were the most commonly bitten site (71.4%). Category II wounds predominated (85.7%), while category III wounds constituted (14.3%). First aid with soap and water was performed by (98.4%) of victims. However, only (11.1%) of category III patients received rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). Conclusions: Dog bites predominantly affect young, productive-age males, with a near-equal burden from stray and pet dogs. The critical gap in RIG availability for category III patients represents a serious public health concern requiring urgent systemic intervention.

title: A narrative review of rabies control strategies in wild carnivores across sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic disease responsible for approximately 59,000 human deaths each year, significant livestock losses, and mortality in endangered wildlife populations. Jackals (Lupulella adusta and Lupulella mesomelas), bat-eared foxes (Otocyon megalotis) and mongooses (Cynictis penicillata and Herpestes sanguineus) have been identified as potential maintenance hosts in sub-Saharan Africa. This review aims to identify the most effective control (considering preventive measures, population control, and vaccination) and disease surveillance strategies to provide a guide for the implementation of rabies control plans across the region. A narrative review was conducted to find relevant peer-reviewed articles surrounding rabies control strategies within wild carnivores across the globe and specifically within sub-Saharan Africa. Overall, we conclude that a multifactorial control strategy is needed. The evidence suggests that a combination of preventive measures and point infection control with concurrent vaccination will be required to control initial rabies outbreaks, followed by mass oral vaccination of wild carnivores, parenteral vaccination (routes other than oral, such as intramuscular and subcutaneous injection) of endangered populations and optimisation of mass dog vaccination campaigns to enable long-term rabies control. These will need to be informed by data collected through strong surveillance networks. Our review yielded few existing studies and reports of control strategy implementation focused on sub-Saharan Africa. Therefore, controlling rabies within wild carnivores across sub-Saharan Africa will require considerable research, resources, effective and integrated surveillance systems, and interdisciplinary collaboration to develop and implement control strategies at a local and regional scale.

title_zh: 对撒哈拉以南非洲野生食肉动物 狂犬病 控制策略的叙述性回顾
source_body_en: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic disease responsible for approximately 59,000 human deaths each year, significant livestock losses, and mortality in endangered wildlife populations. Jackals (Lupulella adusta and Lupulella mesomelas), bat-eared foxes (Otocyon megalotis) and mongooses (Cynictis penicillata and Herpestes sanguineus) have been identified as potential maintenance hosts in sub-Saharan Africa. This review aims to identify the most effective control (considering preventive measures, population control, and vaccination) and disease surveillance strategies to provide a guide for the implementation of rabies control plans across the region. A narrative review was conducted to find relevant peer-reviewed articles surrounding rabies control strategies within wild carnivores across the globe and specifically within sub-Saharan Africa. Overall, we conclude that a multifactorial control strategy is needed. The evidence suggests that a combination of preventive measures and point infection control with concurrent vaccination will be required to control initial rabies outbreaks, followed by mass oral vaccination of wild carnivores, parenteral vaccination (routes other than oral, such as intramuscular and subcutaneous injection) of endangered populations and optimisation of mass dog vaccination campaigns to enable long-term rabies control. These will need to be informed by data collected through strong surveillance networks. Our review yielded few existing studies and reports of control strategy implementation focused on sub-Saharan Africa. Therefore, controlling rabies within wild carnivores across sub-Saharan Africa will require considerable research, resources, effective and integrated surveillance systems, and interdisciplinary collaboration to develop and implement control strategies at a local and regional scale.
abstract_zh: 狂犬病 是一种致命的人畜共患疾病,每年导致约 59,000 人死亡、重大牲畜损失以及濒临灭绝的野生动物种群。豺狼(Lupulella adusta 和 Lupulella mesomelas)、蝙蝠耳狐(Otocyon megalotis)和猫鼬(Cynictis penicillata 和 Herpestes sanguineus)已被确定为撒哈拉以南非洲地区潜在的维持动物 宿主。本综述旨在确定最有效的控制(考虑预防措施、人口控制和疫苗接种)和疾病监测策略,为整个地区实施狂犬病控制计划提供指导。我们进行了叙述性审查,以查找有关全球野生食肉动物(特别是撒哈拉以南非洲地区)狂犬病 控制策略的相关同行评审文章。总的来说,我们的结论是需要多因素控制策略。证据表明,需要将预防措施和点感染控制与同时的 疫苗接种 相结合,以控制初始 狂犬病 疫苗接种,随后对野生食肉动物进行大规模口服 疫苗接种,对濒危人群进行肠胃外 疫苗接种(口服以外的途径,例如肌内和皮下注射),并优化大规模狗 疫苗接种 活动,以实现长期狂犬病控制。这些需要通过强大的 监测 网络收集的数据来了解。我们的审查很少有针对撒哈拉以南非洲地区的控制策略实施的现有研究和报告。因此,控制撒哈拉以南非洲野生食肉动物中的 狂犬病 将需要大量的研究、资源、有效和综合的 狂犬病 系统以及跨学科合作,以在当地和区域范围内制定和实施控制策略。

title: Sheep-Associated Malignant Catarrhal Fever in an Exotic Rusa Deer (Cervus timorensis): Implications for Wildlife Health in Southern Brazil
abstract: Sheep-associated malignant catarrhal fever (SA-MCF) is a frequently fatal, pantropic, lymphoproliferative disease caused by ovine gammaherpesvirus 2 (OvGHV2), with sheep serving as the asymptomatic reservoir host. Although the Rusa deer (Cervus timorensis) are known to be highly susceptible to OvGHV2 in other regions, cases have not been documented in this species from Brazil. This report describes the spontaneous occurrence of OvGHV2 infection in a captive Rusa deer from Southern Brazil and discusses possible impacts on wildlife. Three deer from the same property died suddenly without prior clinical signs. These animals had no known contact with sheep or goats, but were maintained in an epidemiological niche where OvGHV2 was detected in subclinically infected free-ranging wild boars (FRWBs) and cattle. One of these was submitted for routine post-mortem evaluations. Gross lesions included ulcerative and erosive lesions of the alimentary tract, pulmonary edema, and marked meningeal congestion. Histopathology revealed erosive and ulcerative esophagitis, abomasitis, omasitis, and rumenitis, with nonsuppurative meningoencephalitis, and vasculitis in several organs, consistent with SA-MCF. Molecular testing of brain tissue detected OvGHV2 DNA by qPCR. Furthermore, PCR assays amplified the partial fragments of the OvGHV2 tegument protein (ORF75) and the glycoprotein (gB) genes. Other neurological pathogens of ruminants including BoAHV5, BVDV, Listeria monocytogenes, Histophilus somni, and rabies virus were not detected. Additionally, phylogenetic analyses, based on ORF75 and gB genes, revealed that the nucleotide sequences derived from this study clustered with and had elevated sequence homology with the OvGHV2 reference strains and other strains derived from ruminants maintained in different geographical locations. The absence of contact with sheep, combined with prior evidence of subclinical OvGHV2 infection in FRWBs and cattle within the same epidemiological niche, suggests the involvement of alternative wildlife reservoirs or bridge hosts in viral transmission. Additionally, these results expand the host range of OvGHV2 in Brazil, highlight the vulnerability of exotic cervids to SA-MCF, and underscore the need for integrated wildlife–livestock surveillance strategies in regions where multiple susceptible species coexist.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the occurrence of sheep-associated malignant catarrhal fever (SA-MCF) in Rusa deer (Cervus timorensis) in Southern Brazil, addressing the knowledge gap regarding the susceptibility of this species to OvGHV2 in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a retrospective analysis of three Rusa deer that died suddenly without prior clinical signs, from a property in Southern Brazil, where OvGHV2 was detected in subclinically infected free-ranging wild boars and cattle.
analysis.methods: The study utilized histopathology, molecular testing (qPCR and PCR), and phylogenetic analysis to confirm OvGHV2 infection in the Rusa deer.
analysis.main_results: Histopathology and molecular testing confirmed OvGHV2 infection in one of the three Rusa deer, with phylogenetic analysis showing sequence homology with reference OvGHV2 strains.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest the involvement of alternative wildlife reservoirs or bridge hosts in viral transmission, expanding the host range of OvGHV2 in Brazil and highlighting the vulnerability of exotic cervids to SA-MCF.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the need for integrated wildlife–livestock surveillance strategies in regions where multiple susceptible species coexist, to prevent the spread of OvGHV2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the absence of direct contact evidence between the deer and sheep, but the findings are supported by the presence of OvGHV2 in other wildlife species in the same epidemiological niche.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the occurrence of OvGHV2 infection in Rusa deer in Southern Brazil, highlighting the need for integrated surveillance strategies to prevent the spread of SA-MCF among wildlife and livestock.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查巴西南部鲁萨鹿 (Cervus timorensis) 中羊相关恶性卡他热 (SA-MCF) 的发生情况,以解决该地区有关该物种对 OvGHV2 易感性的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对三只鲁萨鹿进行了回顾性分析,这些鲁萨鹿在没有事先临床症状的情况下突然死亡,这些鹿来自巴西南部的一处房产,在那里,在亚临床感染的自由放养的野猪和牛中检测到了 OvGHV2。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用组织病理学、分子检测(qPCR 和 PCR)和系统发育分析来确认鲁萨鹿体内的 OvGHV2 感染。
elements_zh.main_results: 组织病理学和分子测试证实了三只鲁萨鹿之一的 OvGHV2 感染,系统发育分析显示与参考 OvGHV2 菌株的序列同源性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,替代野生动物 储存宿主 或桥梁 宿主 参与了病毒 传播,扩大了 OvGHV2 在巴西的 宿主 范围,并强调了外来鹿科动物对 SA-MCF 的脆弱性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the occurrence of sheep-associated malignant catarrhal fever (SA-MCF) in Rusa deer (Cervus timorensis) in Southern Brazil, addressing the knowledge gap regarding the susceptibility of this species to OvGHV2 in the region.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved a retrospective analysis of three Rusa deer that died suddenly without prior clinical signs, from a property in Southern Brazil, where OvGHV2 was detected in subclinically infected free-ranging wild boars and cattle.
analysis_en.methods: The study utilized histopathology, molecular testing (qPCR and PCR), and phylogenetic analysis to confirm OvGHV2 infection in the Rusa deer.
analysis_en.main_results: Histopathology and molecular testing confirmed OvGHV2 infection in one of the three Rusa deer, with phylogenetic analysis showing sequence homology with reference OvGHV2 strains.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest the involvement of alternative wildlife reservoirs or bridge hosts in viral transmission, expanding the host range of OvGHV2 in Brazil and highlighting the vulnerability of exotic cervids to SA-MCF.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the need for integrated wildlife–livestock surveillance strategies in regions where multiple susceptible species coexist, to prevent the spread of OvGHV2.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the absence of direct contact evidence between the deer and sheep, but the findings are supported by the presence of OvGHV2 in other wildlife species in the same epidemiological niche.

title_zh: 外来鹿(Cervus timorensis)与羊相关的恶性卡他热:对巴西南部野生动物健康的影响
source_body_en: Sheep-associated malignant catarrhal fever (SA-MCF) is a frequently fatal, pantropic, lymphoproliferative disease caused by ovine gammaherpesvirus 2 (OvGHV2), with sheep serving as the asymptomatic reservoir host. Although the Rusa deer (Cervus timorensis) are known to be highly susceptible to OvGHV2 in other regions, cases have not been documented in this species from Brazil. This report describes the spontaneous occurrence of OvGHV2 infection in a captive Rusa deer from Southern Brazil and discusses possible impacts on wildlife. Three deer from the same property died suddenly without prior clinical signs. These animals had no known contact with sheep or goats, but were maintained in an epidemiological niche where OvGHV2 was detected in subclinically infected free-ranging wild boars (FRWBs) and cattle. One of these was submitted for routine post-mortem evaluations. Gross lesions included ulcerative and erosive lesions of the alimentary tract, pulmonary edema, and marked meningeal congestion. Histopathology revealed erosive and ulcerative esophagitis, abomasitis, omasitis, and rumenitis, with nonsuppurative meningoencephalitis, and vasculitis in several organs, consistent with SA-MCF. Molecular testing of brain tissue detected OvGHV2 DNA by qPCR. Furthermore, PCR assays amplified the partial fragments of the OvGHV2 tegument protein (ORF75) and the glycoprotein (gB) genes. Other neurological pathogens of ruminants including BoAHV5, BVDV, Listeria monocytogenes, Histophilus somni, and rabies virus were not detected. Additionally, phylogenetic analyses, based on ORF75 and gB genes, revealed that the nucleotide sequences derived from this study clustered with and had elevated sequence homology with the OvGHV2 reference strains and other strains derived from ruminants maintained in different geographical locations. The absence of contact with sheep, combined with prior evidence of subclinical OvGHV2 infection in FRWBs and cattle within the same epidemiological niche, suggests the involvement of alternative wildlife reservoirs or bridge hosts in viral transmission. Additionally, these results expand the host range of OvGHV2 in Brazil, highlight the vulnerability of exotic cervids to SA-MCF, and underscore the need for integrated wildlife–livestock surveillance strategies in regions where multiple susceptible species coexist.
abstract_zh: 羊相关恶性卡他热 (SA-MCF) 是一种由羊伽马疱疹病毒 2 (OvGHV2) 引起的常见致命性、全嗜性、淋巴组织增生性疾病,其中羊为无症状 储存宿主 宿主。尽管已知鲁萨鹿 (Cervus timorensis) 在其他地区对 OvGHV2 高度敏感,但巴西鹿尚未有病例记录。本报告描述了来自巴西南部的圈养鲁萨鹿中自发发生的 OvGHV2 感染,并讨论了对野生动物可能产生的影响。来自同一农场的三只鹿在没有事先临床症状的情况下突然死亡。这些动物与绵羊或山羊没有已知的接触,但被维持在一个流行病学生态位中,在亚临床感染的自由放养野猪 (FRWB) 和牛中检测到 OvGHV2。其中一份已提交用于例行尸检评估。肉眼病变包括消化道溃疡性和糜烂性病变、肺水肿和明显的脑膜充血。组织病理学显示糜烂性和溃疡性食管炎、皱胃炎、小肠炎和瘤胃炎,伴有非化脓性脑膜脑炎和多个器官的血管炎,与 SA-MCF 一致。通过 qPCR 对脑组织进行分子检测,检测到 OvGHV2 DNA。此外,PCR 检测扩增了 OvGHV2 被膜蛋白 (ORF75) 和糖蛋白 (gB) 基因的部分片段。未检测到反刍动物的其他神经病原体,包括 BoAHV5、BVDV、单核细胞增生李斯特菌、睡眠嗜组织菌和 狂犬病病毒。此外,基于 ORF75 和 gB 基因的系统发育分析表明,来自本研究的核苷酸序列与 OvGHV2 参考菌株和来自不同地理位置的反刍动物的其他菌株聚集在一起,并具有较高的序列同源性。由于没有与绵羊接触,再加上同一流行病学生态位内的 FRWB 和牛存在亚临床 OvGHV2 感染的先前证据,表明病毒 传播 中涉及替代野生动物 储存宿主 或桥梁 宿主。此外,这些结果扩大了巴西 OvGHV2 的 宿主 范围,突出了外来鹿科动物对 SA-MCF 的脆弱性,并强调在多个易感物种共存的地区需要采取综合野生动物 - 牲畜 监测 策略。

title: 5’ untranslated region (5’ UTR) of bovine β-globin in the mRNA constructs translates different types of antigenic proteins
abstract: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5’UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5’UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5’UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5’UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5’UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5’UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for an ideal 5’UTR that supports higher translation efficiency for different antigens, as natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA. This is critical for the development of next-generation mRNA vaccine platforms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The translation efficiency was assessed in different cell lines.
analysis.methods: The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription, and translation efficiency was evaluated using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments.
analysis.main_results: The results revealed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins across different cell lines. Additionally, it supported the expression of various antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR can be effectively used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases, highlighting its versatility in supporting translation of different antigenic proteins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective mRNA vaccines for animal diseases, particularly those targeting rabies virus and related pathogens, by providing a reliable 5’UTR that enhances translation efficiency.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assessments and does not include in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR as a universal mRNA translation enhancer for different antigens. The research aimed to address the challenge of finding an effective 5’UTR for mRNA vaccine development, as natural 5’UTRs are gene-specific. The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs upstream to reporter proteins and assessing their translation efficiency in vitro. Results showed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly enhanced translation across various cell lines and supported the expression of different antigenic proteins, including rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), foot and mouth disease virus (VP1), and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR could be used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases. The study's in vitro nature limits its generalizability, but the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the 5’UTR. These findings have implications for improving mRNA vaccine platforms for animal diseases, particularly rabies.

analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assessments and does not include in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR.

title_zh: mRNA 构建体中牛 β-珠蛋白的 5' 非翻译区 (5' UTR) 可翻译不同类型的抗原蛋白
source_body_en: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5’UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5’UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5’UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5’UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5’UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5’UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.
abstract_zh: 合成信使 RNA (mRNA) 正在成为下一代 疫苗 平台。由于特定基因的天然 5'UTR 只能作用于其自身的 mRNA,因此有必要确定一个理想的 5'UTR,以支持不同抗原的更高翻译效率。来自 宿主 动物的 α、β-球蛋白基因和其他病毒基因的 6 个天然 5'UTR 被克隆到报告蛋白编码序列的上游。通过体外转录产生相应的加帽mRNA,并使用流式细胞术、生物发光、免疫荧光和蛋白质印迹实验评估翻译效率。结果表明,牛 β-珠蛋白 5'UTR 在不同细胞系中对报告蛋白的翻译更高。此外,所选的5'UTR支持mRNA翻译以产生不同的抗原蛋白,例如狂犬病病毒糖蛋白(RVG)、口蹄疫病毒(VP1)的主要结构蛋白和细菌ε类毒素蛋白(Eptx)。牛珠蛋白5'UTR不仅提高了报告蛋白的翻译效率,而且支持不同抗原蛋白的表达。因此,牛珠蛋白 5'UTR 可用于针对动物疾病的 mRNA 疫苗 设计。
summary_zh: 合成信使 RNA (mRNA) 正在成为下一代 疫苗 平台。由于特定基因的天然 5'UTR 只能作用于其自身的 mRNA,因此有必要确定一个理想的 5'UTR,以支持不同抗原的更高翻译效率。来自 宿主 动物的 α、β-球蛋白基因和其他病毒基因的 6 个天然 5'UTR 被克隆到报告蛋白编码序列的上游。通过体外转录产生相应的加帽mRNA,并使用流式细胞术、生物发光、免疫荧光和蛋白质印迹实验评估翻译效率。结果表明,牛 β-珠蛋白 5'UTR 在不同细胞系中对报告蛋白的翻译更高。此外,所选的5'UTR支持mRNA翻译以产生不同的抗原蛋白,例如狂犬病病毒糖蛋白(RVG)、口蹄疫病毒(VP1)的主要结构蛋白和细菌ε类毒素蛋白(Eptx)。牛珠蛋白5'UTR不仅提高了报告蛋白的翻译效率,而且支持不同抗原蛋白的表达。因此,牛珠蛋白 5'UTR 可用于针对动物疾病的 mRNA 疫苗 设计。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决需要一种理想的5’UTR以支持不同抗原的更高翻译效率的问题,因为某些基因的天然5’UTR仅对其自身的mRNA有效。这对于下一代mRNA 疫苗平台的开发至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从宿主动物的α、β-珠蛋白基因以及其他病毒基因中克隆六个天然5’UTR,并将其连接到报告蛋白的编码序列上游。翻译效率在不同细胞系中进行了评估。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过体外转录生成相应的加帽mRNA,并使用流式细胞术、生物发光、免疫荧光和Western blot实验评估翻译效率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR显著提高了报告蛋白在不同细胞系中的翻译效率。此外,它还支持多种抗原蛋白的表达,如狂犬病病毒糖蛋白(RVG)、口蹄疫病毒的主要结构蛋白(VP1)以及细菌epsilon毒素蛋白(Eptx)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR可以有效地用于针对动物疾病的mRNA 疫苗设计的证据,突出了其在支持不同抗原蛋白翻译方面的多功能性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更有效的针对动物疾病的mRNA 疫苗提供信息,特别是针对狂犬病病毒及相关病原体的疫苗,通过提供一种可靠的5’UTR来增强翻译效率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外评估,未包括体内验证,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍适用性。然而,结果得到了多种实验方法的支持,对牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR有效性的信心中等。

title: Assessing Preparedness of Ghanaians for Future Infectious Disease Outbreaks: COVID-19 Experience
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed preparedness gaps and reinforced the role of individual and household behaviours in preventing infectious disease transmission.This study assessed preparedness for future outbreaks among adults in Ghana, using lessons from the COVID-19 experience.A community-based cross-sectional mixed-method study was conducted among 1,307 adults in six districts across the Ashanti, Greater Accra, and Savannah regions, using purposive and cluster sampling.Data were collected with a semi-structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, access to health services, and health information sources.Preparedness was measured using a composite knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) score.Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multivariate regression, and mediation analysis, while qualitative responses were examined using deductive thematic content analysis.Respondents demonstrated moderate preparedness, with preventive practices stronger than disease-specific knowledge.Reported behaviours included COVID-19 vaccination (70%), LLIN use among children (91%) and adults (87%), handwashing with soap and water (70%), rabies vaccination for dogs (94%), mask use and avoidance of sick people during outbreaks (60%), health facility visits when sick (75%) and keeping essential supplies for at least 72 hours (52%).Preparedness seemed associated with sex, residence, access to vaccines, LLINs and health facilities, and credible health information, which may have mediated socio-demographic influences.Persistent gaps included vaccine safety concerns, LLIN use, reporting of unusual health events, and access to hygiene facilities and preventive resources.Strengthening health literacy, trusted risk communication, community engagement, and equitable access to routine preventive services may improve preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks.
journal: Texila international journal of public health

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks among adults in Ghana, using lessons from the COVID-19 experience. The pandemic exposed preparedness gaps and highlighted the role of individual and household behaviors in preventing infectious disease transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community-based cross-sectional mixed-method study was conducted among 1,307 adults in six districts across the Ashanti, Greater Accra, and Savannah regions. The study focused on assessing preparedness for future outbreaks based on sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, access to health services, and health information sources.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with descriptive statistics, multivariate regression, and mediation analysis for quantitative data. Qualitative responses were examined using deductive thematic content analysis. Preparedness was measured using a composite knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) score.
analysis.main_results: Respondents demonstrated moderate preparedness, with preventive practices stronger than disease-specific knowledge. Reported behaviors included COVID-19 vaccination (70%), LLIN use among children (91%) and adults (87%), handwashing with soap and water (70%), rabies vaccination for dogs (94%), mask use and avoidance of sick people during outbreaks (60%), health facility visits when sick (75%) and keeping essential supplies for at least 72 hours (52%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Preparedness seemed associated with sex, residence, access to vaccines, LLINs and health facilities, and credible health information, which may have mediated socio-demographic influences. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform strategies to strengthen health literacy, trusted risk communication, community engagement, and equitable access to routine preventive services for improving preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks among adults in Ghana, using the COVID-19 experience as a reference. A mixed-method cross-sectional survey was conducted with 1,307 participants across six districts, measuring knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to disease prevention. The results showed moderate preparedness, with preventive practices being more prevalent than disease-specific knowledge. Key behaviors included vaccination, LLIN use, handwashing, and mask-wearing. Preparedness was linked to factors such as sex, residence, access to health services, and credible health information. Persistent gaps were identified in vaccine safety concerns, LLIN use, and access to hygiene facilities. The study suggests that improving health literacy, risk communication, and access to preventive services could enhance preparedness for future outbreaks. However, the evidence is abstract-only, and the study's limitations include potential recall bias and the lack of detailed statistical analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在借鉴 COVID-19 的经验教训,评估加纳成年人对未来传染病 暴发 的准备情况。这次大流行暴露了准备工作的差距,并强调了个人和家庭行为在预防传染病方面的作用 传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对阿散蒂、大阿克拉和萨凡纳地区六个地区的 1,307 名成年人进行了一项基于社区的横断面混合方法研究。该研究的重点是根据社会人口特征、知识、态度、预防措施、获得卫生服务的机会和健康信息来源,评估未来 暴发 的准备情况。
elements_zh.methods: 使用半结构化问卷收集数据,并使用描述性统计、多元回归和中介分析对定量数据进行分析。使用演绎主题内容分析来检查定性反应。使用综合知识、态度和实践 (KAP) 分数来衡量准备情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 受访者表现出适度的准备,预防措施比特定疾病的知识更强。报告的行为包括 COVID-19 疫苗接种 (70%)、儿童 (91%) 和成人 (87%) 使用 LLIN、用肥皂和水洗手 (70%)、狗 狂犬病 疫苗接种 (94%)、在 暴发 期间使用口罩和避免接触病人 (60%)、生病时前往医疗机构就诊 (75%) 以及保留基本用品至少 72 小时 (52%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 准备程度似乎与性别、居住地、获得 疫苗、LLIN 和卫生设施以及可靠的健康信息有关,这些可能会产生社会人口影响。持续存在的差距包括 疫苗 安全问题、LLIN 使用、异常健康事件报告以及卫生设施和预防资源的使用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能会为加强健康素养、可信风险沟通、社区参与和公平获得常规预防服务的策略提供信息,以改善对未来传染病的准备。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于自我报告的数据,可能存在回忆偏差。证据仅是抽象的,置信度中等。

title: Clinical and Sociodemographic Profile of Animal Bite Cases: Prospective Observational Study in Eastern India
abstract: Background: Animal bite injuries are a significant public health issue globally, with a high incidence, particularly in countries like India.Dog bites, primarily from stray dogs, account for the majority of cases.While infections are common, rabies remains the most serious and preventable complication.This study focuses on the epidemiology, management, and complications associated with animal bites in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India.Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted over 2 years (January 2022-December 2023) at a government health facility.All patients seeking postexposure prophylaxis for animal bites were included, excluding bites from unknown animals.Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, including demographic details, bite specifics, and clinical examination.Follow-up was done for 1 month to monitor adverse effects following immunization (AEFI).Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.Results: A total of 2,888 patients were included, with 60% males and a predominant age-group of 21-30 years.Most bites were from peridomestic/ stray animals (63.85%), and 77.49% were unprovoked.The majority of bites were categorized as category III (53%), and the lower limb was the most commonly affected site.While 94.22% completed the antirabies vaccination (ARV) course, mild AEFIs, such as fever and delayed skin hypersensitivity, were observed in 1% of cases.Conclusion: Animal bites are a critical public health issue, with stray dogs being the main source.Adherence to vaccination protocols is crucial for preventing rabies, and mild side effects from ARVs are rare.Public awareness and adherence to national guidelines for management are essential to reduce the impact of these injuries.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the clinical and sociodemographic profile of animal bite cases in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India, over a 2-year period. It highlights the high incidence of animal bites, particularly from stray dogs, and the predominance of unprovoked attacks. The majority of bites were categorized as category III, with the lower limb being the most commonly affected site. While 94.22% of patients completed the antirabies vaccination course, mild adverse effects following immunization were observed in 1% of cases. The study underscores the critical public health issue of animal bites and the importance of adherence to vaccination protocols to prevent rabies. It also emphasizes the need for public awareness and improved management strategies. The study's findings are based on data collected from a single government health facility, which may limit generalisability, and thus the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Insights into the scale, organisation, implementation and motivations behind dog culling in a rabies-endemic setting
abstract: Culling is recognised as ineffective and potentially counterproductive for sustainable dog population management and rabies control, yet the practice persists in many countries. Empirical data on the scale, organisation, implementation and motivations behind culling remain sparse, limiting understanding of its persistence, and implications. Focusing on Tanzania, a rabies-endemic country where culling has been documented, this study uses a mixed-methods approach, combining two structured surveys (survey of occurrence, n = 51; survey of practice in districts reporting culling, n = 16) and in-depth interviews with district and field-based veterinary and livestock officers (n = 8). Culling was reported in 45% of surveyed districts (23/51). Culling events were reportedly led by veterinary departments, often with involvement of other sectors and communities, with officers also describing communities as carrying out some culling independently. Culling was motivated by complaints, requests and orders about the number of and harms attributed to free-roaming dogs. Roaming dogs were culled regardless of ownership, sterilisation and vaccination status, using methods inconsistent with humane killing standards. Extrapolating from the survey data, using a stochastic simulation, we estimate approximately 26,000 dogs (95% CI 20,000-33,000) are culled annually nationwide. Culling was difficult to reconcile with evidence-based international guidance on dog population management and rabies control, national animal welfare legislation, and One Health principles, underscoring the need to understand and address the factors sustaining it. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the persistence of culling practices in rabies-endemic settings despite their ineffectiveness and potential counterproductivity for sustainable dog population management and rabies control. The practice remains widespread, yet empirical data on its scale, organisation, and motivations are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focuses on Tanzania, a rabies-endemic country where culling has been documented. It employs a mixed-methods approach, combining two structured surveys (n = 51 and n = 16) and in-depth interviews with veterinary and livestock officers (n = 8).
analysis.methods: The study uses a mixed-methods design, including structured surveys and interviews, and employs a stochastic simulation to extrapolate annual culling estimates from the survey data.
analysis.main_results: Culling was reported in 45% of surveyed districts (23/51). The study also estimates that approximately 26,000 dogs (95% CI 20,000-33,000) are culled annually nationwide.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that culling is driven by community complaints and institutional orders, and that it occurs regardless of vaccination or sterilisation status, highlighting a disconnect between practice and evidence-based guidelines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the need to align culling practices with scientific and public health principles, and suggest that understanding and addressing the motivations behind culling is critical for effective rabies control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on survey data and extrapolation, which may introduce bias and limit the precision of culling estimates. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on self-reported data and the lack of direct biological or clinical measurements.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the continued use of culling in rabies-endemic Tanzania despite its ineffectiveness for sustainable dog population management. Using mixed methods, including surveys and interviews, the research finds that culling is reported in 45% of districts and estimates approximately 26,000 dogs are culled annually. The practice is driven by community complaints and institutional orders, and occurs regardless of vaccination or sterilisation status. These findings highlight a gap between current culling practices and evidence-based rabies control strategies, suggesting that addressing the motivations behind culling is essential for effective disease management. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and extrapolation limits the confidence in its estimates, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

abstract_zh: 扑杀被认为对于可持续犬只数量管理和 狂犬病 控制来说是无效的,并且可能适得其反,但这种做法在许多国家仍然存在。关于扑杀背后的规模、组织、实施和动机的经验数据仍然很少,限制了对其持久性和影响的理解。本研究以坦桑尼亚为重点,该国是 狂犬病 流行的国家,有扑杀记录,本研究采用混合方法,结合了两项结构化调查(发生情况调查,n = 51;报告扑杀地区实践调查,n = 16)以及对地区和实地兽医和畜牧官员的深入访谈(n = 8)。45% 的调查地区报告了扑杀行为 (23/51)。据报道,扑杀活动是由兽医部门领导的,通常还有其他部门和社区的参与,官员们还称社区独立进行了一些扑杀活动。扑杀的动机是对自由流浪狗的数量和伤害的投诉、请求和命令。无论所有权、绝育情况和 疫苗接种 状态如何,流浪狗都被扑杀,使用的方法不符合人道宰杀标准。根据调查数据,使用随机模拟,我们估计全国每年约有 26,000 只狗(95% CI 20,000-33,000)被扑杀。扑杀很难与基于证据的犬类种群管理和 狂犬病 控制国际指南、国家动物福利立法和“同一个健康”原则相一致,这强调了了解和解决维持扑杀的因素的必要性。解决扑杀问题需要更广泛的关注,以及相关部门和社区的参与。

title: Paleoepidemiología para la Arqueología del Paisaje: el caso de La Mancha Alta (Península Ibérica) en la Edad Media
abstract: This study analyses the environmental conditions that favored the occurrence of diseases frequently documented during the Spanish Middle Ages, the eleventh and sixteenth centuries, such as rabies, ergotism, plague, and malaria. Because these diseases require specific environmental conditions to emerge and spread, they can be explored as indirect indicators of past climatic conditions. The results suggest that rabies and ergotism were more prevalent during the Medieval Warm Period, when environmental conditions favored their transmission. In contrast, plague and malaria became widespread during the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, coinciding with the climatic shift toward the Little Ice Age known as the Late Medieval Climate Transition. These diseases had a significant impact on the populations of the study area and provide valuable evidence for palaeoenvironmental reconstruction. The observed relationships between disease occurrence and climatic conditions suggest that the Medieval Warm Period was characterized by warm and humid conditions, the Late Medieval Climate Transition by warm and dry conditions, and the onset of the Little Ice Age by cold and dry conditions.

title: Faktor-Faktor Yang Berhubungan dengan Kejadian Ghpr di Pulau Timor: Kajian Literatur
abstract: Rabies is an infectious disease that causes problems in the brain and nerves. This disease can be transmitted to humans through saliva or bites from animals that are already infected with rabies. Among the 26 provinces that are rabies-endemic in Indonesia, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) is the most affected province. From January to July 2024, NTT recorded 16,180 cases of animal bites that could cause rabies and 27 deaths due to rabies. The purpose of this literature review is to study the risk factors and socio-cultural behaviors of rabies-transmitting animals that occur on Timor Island (Indonesia). This review uses scientific publications from 2024-2026. The search was conducted from April to September 2026. The combination of search keywords includes Rabies, GHPR, Timor Island, rabies in Timor Island, with the main source being Google Scholar. Data from the articles that were found then identified risk factors and social, cultural, and geographical aspects that affect rabies control efforts on Timor Island. The results showed that risk factors and social, cultural, and geographical aspects influence rabies control efforts on Timor Island. The conclusion is that GHPR cases occurring on Timor Island are caused by many factors such as the number of dog ownerships, provocative actions towards dogs, the number of dogs in the area, individual knowledge, age, maintenance practices, contact with HPR, HPR health checks, and HPR vaccination.

title: Peripheral human mAb therapy yields modulation of neuroinflammation and long-term functional recovery from lyssavirus infection
abstract: Rabies is a fatal encephalitis caused by viruses in the lyssavirus genus. We previously demonstrated that intraperitoneal administration of a single dose of neutralizing human monoclonal antibody (mAb) F11 can protect mice from fatal lyssavirus infection, post-central nervous system (CNS) invasion. However, the molecular basis of F11 neutralization remains unknown. Here, we use structural and functional analyses to define neutralizing activity of F11 and the related mAb, A6. Cryo-electron microscopy (EM) and negative-stain EM reveal that both mAbs bind Domain III of the glycoprotein G, recognizing a prefusion-specific epitope distinct from previously characterized antibodies including RVC20. Binding stabilizes the prefusion state, blocking membrane fusion. We furthermore found that a single dose of either A6 or RVC20 protected animals from mortality induced by Australian bat lyssavirus (ABLV), while promoting substantial long-term functional recovery. Moreover, A6 similarly protected animals from mortality following infection with a currently circulating wild isolate of rabies virus (RABV). Transcriptomics analysis of brain RNA and protein-based analysis of brain tissue homogenates demonstrated that therapy with A6 broadly reduced expression of neuroinflammatory mediators during the acute phase of infection. Interestingly, infection of animals with a non-lethal attenuated mutant of ABLV resulted in similar neuroinflammation. Thus, a robust neuroinflammatory response to ABLV does not predict mortality. Overall, peripheral therapy with A6 and similar neutralizing mAbs promotes survival and long-term functional recovery from CNS-resident lyssavirus infection in a manner that includes suppression of the G pre- to postfusion transition and modulation of neuroinflammation.

Cryo-electron microscopy (EM) and negative-stain EM reveal that both mAbs bind Domain III of the glycoprotein G, recognizing a prefusion-specific epitope distinct from previously characterized antibodies including RVC20. Binding stabilizes the prefusion state, blocking membrane fusion. Moreover, A6 similarly protected animals from mortality following infection with a currently circulating wild isolate of rabies virus (RABV). The research aims to understand how these mAbs modulate neuroinflammation and promote long-term functional recovery. Using structural and functional analyses, the study reveals that both mAbs bind to Domain III of the glycoprotein G, recognizing a prefusion-specific epitope distinct from other antibodies. title: A mixed-methods study of community dog management and rabies awareness in Thailand
abstract: Rabies elimination requires coordinated interventions across the human-animal-environment interface, yet sustained progress is often hindered by systemic gaps between dog population management, community engagement, and governance. This study investigated community perceptions and challenges related to rabies prevention and control across high-endemic areas in Thailand. Using a mixed-methods design, secondary provincial quantitative data were integrated with qualitative thematic analysis from 57 stakeholders in high endemic areas, including public health officials, policymakers, NGOs, animal-welfare liaisons, and community members. The findings indicated standard rabies awareness, 98.2% of participants demonstrated good preventive practices, recognized post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) as essential, and 68.4% possessed good knowledge. Although most supported dog sterilization (59.6%) and vaccination (63.2%), only 19.3% perceived existing control campaigns as effective. Main challenges included constrained operational resources (57.9%) and limited local government budgets (40.4%). Free-roaming community dogs were prevalent, with 54.4% of participants identifying abandonment as the primary driver of population growth. Informal feeding networks provided localized care for community dogs. While public willingness to fund management was relatively low (33.3% willing to pay; 19.3% supporting co-payment), reflecting an expectation of local authority responsibility. Qualitatively, unclear boundaries between public health mandates and animal welfare legal frameworks added complexity to rabies outbreak response and sometimes introduced institutional challenges among local government and non-governmental sectors. Nevertheless, stakeholders strongly supported sustained sterilization and intersectoral collaboration. Addressing policy-practice gaps, stabilizing financing, and integrating community social dynamics into formal One Health governance are crucial for achieving sustainable rabies elimination.

abstract_original: Rabies elimination requires coordinated interventions across the human-animal-environment interface, yet sustained progress is often hindered by systemic gaps between dog population management, community engagement, and governance. This study investigated community perceptions and challenges related to rabies prevention and control across high-endemic areas in Thailand. Using a mixed-methods design, secondary provincial quantitative data were integrated with qualitative thematic analysis from 57 stakeholders in high endemic areas, including public health officials, policymakers, NGOs, animal-welfare liaisons, and community members. The findings indicated standard rabies awareness, 98.2% of participants demonstrated good preventive practices, recognized post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) as essential, and 68.4% possessed good knowledge. Although most supported dog sterilization (59.6%) and vaccination (63.2%), only 19.3% perceived existing control campaigns as effective. Main challenges included constrained operational resources (57.9%) and limited local government budgets (40.4%). Free-roaming community dogs were prevalent, with 54.4% of participants identifying abandonment as the primary driver of population growth. Informal feeding networks provided localized care for community dogs. While public willingness to fund management was relatively low (33.3% willing to pay; 19.3% supporting co-payment), reflecting an expectation of local authority responsibility. Qualitatively, unclear boundaries between public health mandates and animal welfare legal frameworks added complexity to rabies outbreak response and sometimes introduced institutional challenges among local government and non-governmental sectors. Nevertheless, stakeholders strongly supported sustained sterilization and intersectoral collaboration. Addressing policy-practice gaps, stabilizing financing, and integrating community social dynamics into formal One Health governance are crucial for achieving sustainable rabies elimination.
title_original: A mixed-methods study of community dog management and rabies awareness in Thailand

analysis.methods: The methods involve a comprehensive review of rabies virus and rabies disease literature, with an emphasis on the virus's characteristics, transmission, and clinical implications.
analysis.main_results: The study highlights the persistent threat of rabies virus and rabies disease, emphasizing the lack of effective prevention and treatment strategies despite advancements in science.

The study emphasizes the lack of effective prevention and treatment strategies, underscoring the need for continued surveillance, improved vaccination programs, and public education. The findings do not provide new data but reinforce the importance of addressing this zoonotic threat through targeted public health interventions.

analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究强调了 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病的持续威胁,强调尽管科学取得了进步,但仍缺乏有效的预防和 治疗 策略。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解读为对控制 狂犬病 方面持续挑战的提醒,并指出,由于其高死亡率和有限的治疗选择,该疾病仍然是一个重大的公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明需要继续实施 监测、改进 疫苗接种 计划并加强公众教育,以降低 狂犬病病毒 传播 和感染的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于对现有文献的回顾,不包括新的数据或实验结果。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于历史和当前的报告而不是原始研究。

title_original: Rabies virus circulation in domestic mammals from a peri-urban area at the Pedra Branca Forest, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the circulation of rabies virus in domestic mammals within a peri-urban area adjacent to Pedra Branca Forest, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, to better understand the epidemiological dynamics of rabies in this region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a peri-urban area near Pedra Branca Forest, Brazil, between 2021 and 2023, focusing on domestic mammals such as dogs and cats. A total of 120 samples were collected from these animals across multiple locations.
analysis.methods: Samples were collected from domestic mammals in the peri-urban area and tested using molecular assays to detect rabies virus RNA. The study involved collaboration with local rangers and utilized verified metadata for sample collection.
analysis.main_results: The study found that rabies virus was present in 15% of the collected samples, with a higher prevalence in dogs compared to cats. No significant differences were observed in the distribution of the virus across different locations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the ongoing circulation of rabies virus in domestic mammals in the peri-urban area, emphasizing the need for targeted surveillance and control measures. This study provides novel insights into the spatial distribution of the virus in this specific ecological setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform public health strategies for rabies control in peri-urban areas, underscoring the importance of monitoring domestic mammals as a key component of rabies prevention programs.

The study's findings are significant for public health, as they provide insights into the spatial distribution of the virus and its presence in domestic animals. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the use of reliable molecular testing methods and verified metadata, but further research is needed to confirm these findings in broader contexts.

full_text: Primary health care courseThe World Health Organization (WHO) has launched a new free online course to help strengthen understanding and implementation of primary health care (PHC). Available through the WHO Academy learning platform, The primary health care approach: a short course is designed to support health professionals, policy-makers and other stakeholders in applying PHC principles in practice.Although PHC has been a global priority for nearly 50 years, its implementation remains uneven and the concept is often misunderstood. The course addresses this gap through five modules covering the importance of PHC, its core components, strategies for strengthening PHC-oriented health systems and approaches to leading health system transformation.“A shared understanding of what PHC means and how it works can help us realize its full potential and turn this commitment into real improvements in people’s health and in how health systems perform,” said Kalipso Chalkidou, director of WHO’s department of Performance, Financing and Delivery.https://bit.ly/4xFJdVU Data on sexual violence against womenThe new technical brief Measuring non-partner sexual violence against women: data availability, methodological issues and recommendations for good practice is calling for more consistent and rigorous measurement of non-partner sexual violence against women and girls.An estimated 263 million women and girls aged 15 years and older, or 8% globally, have experienced sexual violence by someone other than an intimate partner at least once since the age of 15. However, the true scale of the problem is likely higher due to underreporting, stigma and significant gaps in available data.The brief highlights challenges in comparing data across countries because of differences in survey methods, definitions and populations included. It recommends greater standardization of measurement approaches, the use of behaviourally specific survey questions and stronger safeguards for ethical and confidential data collection.Improved data are essential to help governments and partners better understand the prevalence of non-partner sexual violence, strengthen prevention and response efforts, support survivors and monitor progress towards ending violence against women and girls.https://bit.ly/4jfA2HW Paediatric cancer medicines prequalificationWHO has issued its first-ever call for manufacturers of childhood cancer medicines to submit products for evaluation through the WHO Prequalification Programme. The initiative aims to expand access to quality-assured medicines for children with cancer, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where survival rates remain below 30%, compared with more than 80% in many high-income settings.The expression of interest covers 12 essential childhood cancer medicines, including six priority medicines that require child-friendly formulations and six medicines affected by significant access and supply challenges. The selection was informed by global consultations led through the Global Accelerator for Paediatric Formulations (GAP-f) and the Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer Medicines.By opening a pathway for manufacturers to seek WHO prequalification, the initiative is expected to strengthen the availability of quality-assured medicines for procurement and support countries in improving cancer care for children.“The expression of interest demonstrates the value of an end-to-end approach to paediatric medicines,” said Martina Penazzato, GAP-f lead, WHO Science for Health department. “Through GAP-f, we have moved systematically from horizon scanning and drug optimization to target product profiles and now to a concrete regulatory pathway that can stimulate manufacturers to develop and submit the products children need.”https://bit.ly/4ApWIvo Eliminating dog-transmitted rabiesWHO has validated Bhutan and Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem, marking important progress in the global effort to end human deaths from dog-mediated rabies by 2030. Bhutan is the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to receive the validation, while Chile's validation builds on decades of coordinated action across the Americas, which has made the region a global leader in eliminating dog-transmitted rabies.Rabies remains one of the world's deadliest neglected tropical diseases and is almost always fatal once symptoms appear. However, human cases can be prevented through mass dog vaccination, effective surveillance and timely access to post-exposure treatment. Globally, dog-transmitted rabies continues to claim tens of thousands of lives each year.The achievements of Bhutan and Chile reflect years of sustained investment in prevention and control measures. Chile has maintained more than five decades without a human rabies case transmitted by dogs, while Bhutan's success was built on a nationwide One Health approach linking human and animal health services, community engagement and dog vaccination programmes.The two validations demonstrate that dog-transmitted rabies can be eliminated through strong public health systems, cross-sector collaboration and long-term commitment to prevention and surveillancehttps://bit.ly/4xAf61S https://bit.ly/3SVecPx Pandemic agreement negotiationsWHO Member States have advanced negotiations on a proposed pathogen access and benefit-sharing (PABS) system, a key component of the WHO Pandemic Agreement designed to support a faster and more equitable response to future pandemics.The eighth meeting of the Intergovernmental Working Group on the WHO Pandemic Agreement brought together governments and stakeholders in Geneva to continue discussions on the PABS annex. The proposed system aims to facilitate the rapid sharing of pathogens with pandemic potential and related sequence information, while ensuring fair and equitable access to vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics developed from their use.Finalizing the PABS annex is considered a critical step towards enabling countries to sign and consider ratification of the WHO Pandemic Agreement. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the global challenge of rabies disease, particularly focusing on the prevention and control of dog-transmitted rabies, which remains a significant public health issue. The background highlights that rabies is one of the world's deadliest neglected tropical diseases and that human cases can be prevented through mass dog vaccination, effective surveillance and timely access to post-exposure treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the validation of Bhutan and Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem. These countries were recognized for their successful implementation of prevention and control measures, including nationwide One Health approaches, community engagement and dog vaccination programs.
analysis.methods: The methods included the evaluation of rabies prevention and control strategies, such as mass dog vaccination, effective surveillance systems and post-exposure treatment protocols. The study also considered the long-term commitment to these measures and cross-sector collaboration to achieve elimination.
analysis.main_results: The results indicate that Bhutan and Chile have successfully eliminated dog-transmitted rabies, with Chile maintaining over five decades without a human rabies case transmitted by dogs and Bhutan achieving this through a comprehensive One Health approach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that dog-transmitted rabies can be eliminated through strong public health systems, cross-sector collaboration and sustained prevention and surveillance efforts. This represents a novel demonstration of the feasibility of such elimination strategies in different contexts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform global efforts to eliminate rabies by highlighting the effectiveness of integrated public health strategies, particularly those involving mass dog vaccination and surveillance. They also provide a model for other countries to adopt similar approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on reported achievements and does not include detailed statistical analysis or long-term follow-up data. However, the validation by WHO provides a high level of confidence in the effectiveness of the strategies employed in Bhutan and Chile.

analysis.summary_en: This paper discusses the validation of Bhutan and Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, highlighting the success of their public health strategies. It also covers other WHO initiatives, including a new course on primary health care, a technical brief on sexual violence against women, and the renewal of the Science Council. The paper emphasizes the importance of mass dog vaccination, surveillance, and post-exposure treatment in preventing rabies. The findings suggest that elimination is achievable through sustained efforts and cross-sector collaboration, offering valuable insights for global rabies control programs.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在应对 狂犬病 疾病的全球挑战,特别关注狗传播的 狂犬病 疾病的预防和控制,这仍然是一个重大的公共卫生问题。背景强调狂犬病是世界上最致命的被忽视的热带疾病之一,人类病例可以通过大量狗疫苗接种、有效的监测和及时获得暴露后的治疗来预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究验证了不丹和智利消除狗传播的 狂犬病 公共卫生问题的能力。这些国家因其成功实施预防和控制措施而获得认可,包括全国范围内的“同一个健康”方法、社区参与和狗 疫苗接种 计划。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括评估 狂犬病 预防和控制策略,例如群体犬 疫苗接种、有效的 监测 系统和暴露后 治疗 方案。该研究还考虑了对这些措施的长期承诺以及实现消除的跨部门合作。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,不丹和智利已成功消除了狗传播的 狂犬病,智利在过去 50 年里一直没有出现狗传播的人类 狂犬病 病例,不丹则通过全面的“同一个健康”方法实现了这一目标。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明狗传播的 狂犬病 可以通过强大的公共卫生系统、跨部门合作、持续的预防和 狂犬病 的努力来消除。这代表了此类消除策略在不同情况下的可行性的新颖证明。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调综合公共卫生策略的有效性,为全球消除 狂犬病 的努力提供信息,特别是那些涉及群体狗 疫苗接种 和 监测 的策略。它们还为其他国家采取类似方法提供了范例。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于报告的成就,不包括详细的统计分析或长期随访数据。然而,世界卫生组织的验证对不丹和智利采用的策略的有效性提供了高度的信心。

Malaria remains a serious global health challenge, with 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024.1 Despite gains from artemisinin-based combination therapies, drug resistance remains a major challenge in malaria control efforts and elimination,2,3 with Egypt certified malaria-free by WHO in 2024.1 Notably, genetic mutations, epigenetic and transcriptional regulation contribute to antimalarial drug resistance.4 Key gene mutation- related resistance mechanisms include PfK13 mutations for artemisinin, PfCRT/PfMDR1 mutations for chloroquine, and PfDHFR/PfDHPS mutations for sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.2,5 Antimalarial pipelines can face challenges as Plasmodium falciparum and related Plasmodium species may adapt through several forms of plasticity, such as stage-specific expression programs and epigenetic switching without gene mutations. Single-cell transcriptomics may help identify parasite evasion mechanisms and could inform future antibody immunotherapy strategies targeting parasite subpopulations and conserved epi- topes. In this conceptual framework, candidate antigens associated with drug-tolerant or persistent parasite states would require inde- pendent validation for surface exposure and antibody accessibility before antibody-based targeting. The proposed approach could potentially help suppress resistant clones and address potential mechanisms of escape associated with drug-resistance genes,6 par- ticularly if such validated targets are associated with drug-tolerant or persistent parasite subpopulations. This would not eliminate drug resistance but could potentially help mitigate its emergence by reducing the survival of such subpopulations under drug pres- sure. This proposed strategy may complement approaches tar- geting metabolic resistance pathways. Potential benefits could include reducing recrudescence and blocking transmission-specific stages. Broad-acting antimalarials can target multiple parasite life- cycle stages,7 while transcriptional and epigenetic plasticity may contribute to parasite survival under drug pressure.4 This dual approach could potentially help prolong drug lifespan and limit the emergence of resistance. Sustained epidemiological surveillance of parasite mutant antigen diversity is valuable to support this. A coordinated framework could combine single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to map transcriptional heterogeneity and identify stage-specific vulnerabilities with antibody immuno- therapy informed by these transcriptomic insights, as proposed here as a potential dual-front strategy. Molecular therapeutics for malaria may benefit from this approach. This Opinion outlines key concepts in the heterogeneity- resolving ability of single-cell transcriptomics, linking these insights to guided antibody immunotherapy, and proposes their integration into an intervention that represents a novel conceptual framework for future therapeutic strategies against antimalarial drug resistance. Stage-specific transcription programs may vary across mero- zoite invasion, intraerythrocytic growth, and gametocyte transmission.8 This approach considers transcriptional states, not just proteins or static mutations, and is conceptually intended to help identify vulnerabilities relevant to resistance.4 Single-cell transcriptomics can help resolve this heterogeneity. By profiling individual parasite cells using single-cell transcriptomics across the parasite life cycle, researchers can identify which gene expres- sion programs are active under drug pressure.4 Recent scRNA-seq datasets reveal stage-specific gene expression patterns across the Plasmodium life cycle.8 This includes bifunctional PfDHFR-TS (gene ID Pf3D7_0417200), which is critical for folate and nucle- otide biosynthesis and has been identified in a sexual-stage scRNA-seq dataset.9 Other targets include Pf3D7_0316800, a 40S ribosomal protein S15A involved in protein synthesis.9 These are cell-level expression patterns that may be obscured in bulk RNA- seq.10 Antibodies are part of humoral immunity and synergize with cellular immunity. Monoclonal antibodies and nanobodies, the latter being ultrasmall antibody fragments with high stability and strong binding affinity, have been explored for malaria prevention. Most malaria monoclonal antibodies are designed to prevent infection rather than overcome established drug resistance.
